messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: broadcasting for binary ops
parts:
On a completely different topic, I have a question
about how general and how implicit to make binary
operations.

R seems very general here (though I wouldn't even
know where to look it up).

As a prelude, I added binary comparison operators
(<, <=, >, >=, ==, !=) and binary logical operators (&&
and ||) and the unary logical operator (!). They
are defined now in both the parser and in the
C++ implementation to take a pair of double arguments
or a pair of int args (the consequence of this is that
an int and double comparison will promote the int to
a double).

I probably won't get it done and tested for the next
release, but I'd like to be able to use them in the
R style, with code like

real y[K];
int z[K];

z = y > 2 && y < 5;

This requires a version of > that takes an int (or
double) and array as input, and a version of &&
that takes a pair of arrays. This notion is very general.
We could promote row vectors to matrices by replicating
rows or promote column vectors to matrices to by replicating
the column across the matrix. We could also have

vector<vector<double>> == vector<double>

return a vector<vector<int>> by replicating the
vector<double>.

One issue is that we don't have int vectors or matrices,
so if we want to do something like !m, where m is a matrix,
the best we can do is return a 2D array of int.

To do this, we need to do what the Eigen doc calls
"broadcasting" (I can never recall what R calls it):

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TutorialReductionsVisitorsBroadcasting.html#TutorialReductionsVisitorsBroadcastingBroadcasting

I figured out how to do this all with metaprogramming
given just the base operation (I don't know how general
I'll make it, but I'm starting with binary ops).

What I want to know is how general people think the
definitions should be.

We could require the vector to matrix broadcasts,
which seem the most confusing, to be explicit. Or
I could just restrict it to the case where either the
arguments were the same dimensionality or one was
a simple scalar or int.

Once I build the metaprograms, it should be simple to
extend this kind of thing to all of our binary and
unary functions. (Ternary might be tricky.) I'm still
absolutely giddy with delight at how nice our current
probability functions look and how efficient they are.
We don't need as much work for the binary ops, because
they return multivariates, which won't allow us to save
on auto-dif (at least not easily) the way we do in the
probability functions.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] broadcasting for binary ops
parts:
The numpy library for python does a very general form of broadcasting like this.  For a general ND array, al singleton dimensions can get broadcast up to the size of the corresponding dimensions in the other array.  It's a really nice feature, but it is primarily for efficiencies which we are unlikely to realize.

I would say focus on broadcasting for the scalar vs vector/matrix/array case.  This is consistent with what we're already doing for scalar-matrix/vector ops +, -, * and /.

Cheers,
Marcus

On 11/29/12 11:26 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> The numpy library for python does a very general form of broadcasting like this. For a general ND array, al singleton
> dimensions can get broadcast up to the size of the corresponding dimensions in the other array.
Thanks for the pointer -- I'll read up on their design.

> It's a really nice
> feature, but it is primarily for efficiencies which we are unlikely to realize.

It's all coding convenience for us -- it won't be
faster than a loop, unlike the broadcasting you did
for the auto-dif lib.

> I would say focus on broadcasting for the scalar vs vector/matrix/array case. This is consistent with what we're
> already doing for scalar-matrix/vector ops +, -, * and /.

That's what I'm implementing first.

I also thought the more general cases would be confusing
to doc and for users. But they're pretty easy to do, so
they're catnip to a generality-obsessed programmer like me.

- Bob

P.S. I'm also going to add proper conditional if-else statements
and probably while loops and maybe plain old for loops.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] broadcasting for binary ops
parts:
The only major issue with adding broadcasting is that it can sometimes trip up unsuspecting users.  For instance, working with python I've occasionally had bugs that were caused by broadcasting causing expressions to work that probably should have failed due to size mismatches.  This then produced a surprising error somewhere else that was hard to track back to the origin.  A more minor issue is that it may expose Stans weaknesses with indexing, reshaping, etc as people try to do more sophisticated things.

All of that said, I too love generality and it can be an incredibly convenient feature to have for large models.  Being able to avoid multiple for loops to do simple operations is incredibly handy and the rules of it are pretty simple to understand once explained.

Cheers,
Marcus
